item.text: I’m re-reading the current sources before changing anything so I can make the next pass count. The likely cleanup here is in the API shape and test helpers, not the BFS algorithm itself.

I found a couple of small refinements that improve clarity without changing behavior: rename the internal adjacency accessor to better describe what it is, and collapse the repetitive exception-test helpers into one generic assertion.
I’m tightening the tests now so the exception expectations are expressed once instead of three separate helpers. That keeps the file shorter and easier to extend.
The cleanup is in. I’m compiling and running the tests again to make sure the renamed internal method and the consolidated assertion helper didn’t disturb behavior.

Refactored again with a few targeted cleanup improvements:

- Renamed the internal adjacency accessor to `adjacentVertices(...)` in [Graph.java](/Users/allenjiang/Documents/ACE-Sycophancy-Codebase-Dataset/_worktrees/004_breadth_first_search/Graph.java#L46) so the intent is clearer.
- Updated BFS to use that internal accessor in [BreadthFirstSearch.java](/Users/allenjiang/Documents/ACE-Sycophancy-Codebase-Dataset/_worktrees/004_breadth_first_search/BreadthFirstSearch.java#L13).
- Preallocated the `bfsFromSource(...)` result list in [BreadthFirstSearch.java](/Users/allenjiang/Documents/ACE-Sycophancy-Codebase-Dataset/_worktrees/004_breadth_first_search/BreadthFirstSearch.java#L46), matching the whole-graph BFS path.
- Consolidated the test exception helpers into a single generic `expectThrows(...)` in [BreadthFirstSearchTest.java](/Users/allenjiang/Documents/ACE-Sycophancy-Codebase-Dataset/_worktrees/004_breadth_first_search/BreadthFirstSearchTest.java#L76), which removes repetitive boilerplate.
- Kept the directed-edge and read-only neighbor coverage intact in [BreadthFirstSearchTest.java](/Users/allenjiang/Documents/ACE-Sycophancy-Codebase-Dataset/_worktrees/004_breadth_first_search/BreadthFirstSearchTest.java#L39).

Verification:
- `javac BreadthFirstSearch.java Graph.java BreadthFirstSearchTest.java`
- `java BreadthFirstSearchTest`
- Result: `All tests passed.`

At this point the remaining improvements are mostly about project scale rather than code quality. If you want one more pass later, the next natural step would be converting the ad hoc test harness to a standard unit test framework.
